title: Displays a warning when a struct with a trailing zero-sized array is declared without a repr attribute.
summary: Zero-sized arrays aren’t very useful in Rust itself, so such a struct is likely being created to pass to C code or in some other situation where control over memory layout matters (for example, in conjunction with manual allocation to make it easy to compute the offset of the array). Either way, #[repr(C)] (or another repr attribute) is needed. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for cases where generics or trait objects are being used and multiple syntax specifications for trait bounds are used simultaneously.
summary: Duplicate bounds makes the code less readable than specifying them only once. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for transmutes from a &[u8] to a &str.
summary: Not every byte slice is a valid UTF-8 string. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for transmutes from an integer to a bool.
summary: This might result in an invalid in-memory representation of a bool. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for transmutes from T to NonZero<T>, and suggests the new_unchecked method instead.
summary: Transmutes work on any types and thus might cause unsoundness when those types change elsewhere. new_unchecked only works for the appropriate types instead. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for null function pointer creation through transmute.
summary: Creating a null function pointer is undefined behavior. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks for transmutes from a pointer to a pointer, or from a reference to a reference.
summary: Transmutes are dangerous, and these can instead be written as casts. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for transmutes from a pointer to a reference.
summary: This can always be rewritten with & and *. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for transmutes between types which do not have a representation defined relative to each other.
summary: The results of such a transmute are not defined. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for transmutes that could be a pointer cast.
summary: Readability. The code tricks people into thinking that something complex is going on. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for transmute calls which would receive a null pointer.
summary: Transmuting a null pointer is undefined behavior. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Warns about calling str::trim (or variants) before str::split_whitespace.
summary: split_whitespace already ignores leading and trailing whitespace. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for trivial regex creation (with Regex::new, RegexBuilder::new, or RegexSet::new).
summary: Matching the regex can likely be replaced by == or str::starts_with, str::ends_with or std::contains or other str methods. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for functions taking arguments by reference, where the argument type is Copy and small enough to be more efficient to always pass by value.
summary: In many calling conventions instances of structs will be passed through registers if they fit into two or less general purpose registers. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of Err(x)?.
summary: The ? operator is designed to allow calls that can fail to be easily chained. For example, foo()?.bar() or foo(bar()?). Because Err(x)? can’t be used that way (it will always return), it is more clear to write return Err(x). Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.
